program.scope: Implementation and deployment plan; no V5 tasks were executed by preparation of this package.
program.phase_gate_policy: Phase prerequisites are gates, not status assumptions. Tasks are ordered within phase; independent work may be parallelized only with contract/integration ownership. P21 is intentionally not a P22 dependency.

phases.title: Freeze baseline, scope and ownership
phases.exit_gate: G00: exact green baseline, scope freeze, environment inventory and initial CI exist; contradictory runtime claims have an evidence-based resolution or precisely scoped gap. No production data migration starts with unproven recovery.
phases.rollback: Only documentation, branch and nonproduction validation change. Any necessary operational repair has its own reversible runbook; V4 remains the live authority.

phases.title: Extract clean service and repository boundaries
phases.exit_gate: G01: existing UI and game behavior remain equivalent; pure domain and contract tests run independently of HTTP/SQLite; a transaction can span multiple repository operations.
phases.rollback: Retain the legacy adapter and compatibility shims; avoid a mass file move. Revert isolated extraction commits if parity fails.

phases.title: Provision Neon and versioned PostgreSQL schema
phases.exit_gate: G02: schema builds from zero solely through migrations; environments/roles are isolated; actual plan, TLS, region, pool and recovery settings are evidenced.
phases.rollback: Only new empty/nonserving resources are affected. Do not drop existing provider objects automatically; keep V4 production unchanged.

phases.title: Build deterministic SQLite import and proof
phases.exit_gate: G03: representative V4 snapshots import with zero unexplained per-actor/data differences; reruns and interruption recovery preserve identical canonical state and all financial/identity invariants.
phases.rollback: Operate only on source copies and nonserving targets. Preserve immutable source snapshot; reset only explicitly identified disposable targets.

phases.title: Replace production persistence with PostgreSQL adapters
phases.exit_gate: G04: the V5 production path has no SQLite dependency; concurrent spends/settlements/payouts and rollback tests pass with approved behavior.
phases.rollback: V4 stays live. Switch only isolated V5 targets; retain schema-compatible app fallback and additive migrations.

phases.title: Implement actor-centric sessions and credential lifecycle
phases.exit_gate: G05: browser-style, Android-style and iOS-style clients resolve to the same permanent actor; refresh, revocation, provider linking and ticket replay tests pass.
phases.rollback: Keep V4 sessions untouched in live production; stage the new credential system with isolated keys. Compatibility adapters must be versioned before activation.

phases.title: Introduce managed ephemeral coordination
phases.exit_gate: G06: Redis loss is temporary disruption only; all player assets/results/identity remain durable and queues/caches recover.
phases.rollback: V5 staging alone changes; disable/rebuild ephemera without database rollback. Managed service removal never deletes durable player state.

phases.title: Make matchmaking safe across multiple processes
phases.exit_gate: G07: multiple matchers cannot double-assign, double-charge or lose committed entrants; current matching and charge timing remain unchanged.
phases.rollback: Stop new V5 matcher work and rebuild ephemeral queues from durable assignments. Never refund/recharge automatically without the existing transaction policy.

phases.title: Deploy revision-based durable realtime Game Core
phases.exit_gate: G08: acknowledged moves survive process death and resume from committed state on another process; no reset deadline, duplicate effect or split match.
phases.rollback: Drain staging sockets and deploy a schema-compatible previous Core. Database state is retained; no restart-void fallback for valid durable matches.

phases.title: Make tournament and lobby execution durable
phases.exit_gate: G09: crash/concurrent workers cannot double-pay, double-refund or lose escrow; approved tournament and private lobby behavior remains.
phases.rollback: Pause/drain processing without changing player outcomes, deploy compatible code and resume fenced work from PostgreSQL.

phases.title: Extract reliable jobs, notifications and provider retries
phases.exit_gate: G10: unrelated jobs survive API/Core restarts; at-least-once delivery produces idempotent authorized effects and visible recoverable failures.
phases.rollback: Stop worker claims and deploy prior compatible worker; jobs remain in PostgreSQL with recoverable leases/fences.

phases.title: Deploy Vercel account and stateless control plane
phases.exit_gate: G11: Vercel and Core serve the same staging actors with no overlapping economic authority; old client routes remain compatible.
phases.rollback: Roll back only the nonproduction API deployment or a PG-compatible production API. No database rollback accompanies Vercel domain changes.

phases.title: Introduce safe read models and caching
phases.exit_gate: G12: cache/projection loss affects speed, not correctness; private state is never shared-cached or used stale for economic authorization.
phases.rollback: Disable caches and serve correct primary reads; preserve source-of-truth state and rebuild projections.

phases.title: Harden distributed trust boundaries
phases.exit_gate: G13: direct/internal/forged/replayed requests cannot bypass player and service authorization; existing security and gameplay decisions do not regress.
phases.rollback: Rotate/revoke isolated credentials or deploy prior compatible security code; never disable authority checks to restore service.

phases.title: Unify traces, metrics and alert delivery
phases.exit_gate: G14: one player-safe support ID can be traced across API/Core/DB/worker without exposing secrets; critical failure and recovery alerts actually arrive.
phases.rollback: Telemetry failures must not corrupt business transactions; reduce sampling/log volume rather than expose raw data or disable authority checks.

phases.title: Prove independent backups and disaster recovery
phases.exit_gate: G15: independently encrypted material can reconstruct the service data in an isolated PostgreSQL target, including privacy/revocation controls, within measured recovery objectives.
phases.rollback: Never overwrite a live database during a drill. Preserve V4 backups and separate V5 prefixes/keys; restore only to a verified isolated target.

phases.title: Add Core process redundancy and rolling drain
phases.exit_gate: G16: losing one Core process does not destroy a valid committed match; clients reconnect to the surviving process. Same-host deployment is accurately labeled process HA.
phases.rollback: Drain/revert one Core at a time to a compatible image; retain PostgreSQL authority and do not move all traffic to a failed process.

phases.title: Complete independent component CI/CD and release gates
phases.exit_gate: G17: API/Core/worker and native artifacts can be built and released independently under schema/protocol compatibility and evidence gates.
phases.rollback: Use previous compatible images/deployments, not database downgrade. V4 tags/workflows remain retained; never overwrite an immutable release.

phases.title: Complete the dedicated V5 staging platform
phases.exit_gate: G18: all components function together on isolated realistic data; retained browser/client-style flows and rehearsed migration/abort paths pass without affecting V4.
phases.rollback: Only V5 staging is reset/redeployed. Production is never stopped to free staging ports or used as a test database.

phases.title: Measure load, failure recovery and safe degradation
phases.exit_gate: G19: sustainable capacity, latency, headroom and failure behavior are measured at realistic history sizes; no integrity failure under retries, loss or concurrency.
phases.rollback: Stop isolated load clients, reduce admission and restore compatible V5 configuration; do not truncate real data or void games to hide overload.

phases.title: Build, sign and validate Android and iOS applications
phases.exit_gate: G20: actual applications, not adapters alone, build and run the unchanged product against V5; required native/device/provider evidence and distribution status are explicit.
phases.rollback: Keep prior internal/native builds available and backend contracts backward compatible. Do not remove an approved UI feature to bypass a native integration defect.

phases.title: Execute final production authority transfer
phases.exit_gate: G22: V5 is the only live durable production application writer; existing and native clients share it; recovery and operational evidence is green. No dependency on deferred Phase 21.

phases.exit_gate: G23: no production service depends on V4 SQLite. Required history/backups and supported-client/provider compatibility remain available under policy.
